items.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023
items.q: I was taking trumpet lessons from a guy in Chicago Symphony... Charlie Geyer. So you know I was kind of going in that direction through high school and he wanted me to go to Northwestern and study with Vincent Cichowicz

ctx.x: This would have happened to you but I had this fascination with big bands when I was about that age and I remember my parents taking me to see what would have been the Glenn Miller ghost orchestra if you want to use that term, and I played the saxophone and I was staring up at them saying, “That’s what I really want to do.” Did you have that kind of experience?

We — my dad was a trombone player also, so he took me to hear Duke Ellington’s band and then also took me to hear Stan Kenton, probably when I was sixteen or seventeen, both of those I guess. It wasn’t really something I wanted to do was play in a big band. I liked it but it wasn’t — I don’t know it didn’t stir me up to become a lead trumpet player or anything. But at the time I was taking trumpet lessons from a guy in Chicago Symphony so I was playing C trumpet in high school and kind of going in that direction…

Can you recall the first time that you understood that a song, a pop song, could have things added to it like horns, and the first time you ever got a pair of headphones on and had that experience? It’s a tough one. © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
